# 6. BASIC

The language is BBC BASIC 3.10, unchanged. This chapter has the syntax
of every keyword, grouped by what it does; the keywords for files,
graphics and sound are in their own chapters (7, 8, 9). Keywords are
written in capitals; `A%`-`Z%` are the fast resident integer variables.

## 6.1 Variables and operators

#### `VARIABLES`

Names are letters, digits and _ and may be long. Types by suffix:

```
A    real (5 bytes, ~9 digits)
A%   integer (32 bits)
A$   string (up to 255 chars)
```

The integers @% and A% to Z% are resident: they survive RUN, NEW and CLEAR. @% sets the PRINT format; A%, X%, Y% and C% pass registers to CALL and USR.

Arrays: DIM A(10), DIM N$(5,5). Strings keep their space when a new value fits. Space that strings give up is only reclaimed by CLEAR or RUN.

#### `OPERATORS`

Arithmetic: + - * / ^ (power), DIV and MOD (integers). Comparison: = <> < > <= >=, giving TRUE (-1) or FALSE (0). Logical/bitwise: AND OR EOR NOT.

Indirection reads and writes memory:

```
?A       byte at address A
!A       4-byte integer at A
$A       string at A (CR ended)
A?2      byte at A+2
A!4      integer at A+4
```

Example:

```
DIM B% 10:?B%=65:PRINT ?B%
```

Hexadecimal: &FF is 255; PRINT ~X prints X in hexadecimal.

#### `LET`

```
[LET] v=expr
```

Assignment; LET may be left out.

#### `DIM`

```
DIM A(n), B$(x,y)
DIM P% n
```

Declares arrays, or reserves n+1 bytes of memory and puts the address in P%.


## 6.2 Working with programs

#### `AUTO`

```
AUTO [start[,step]]
```

Numbers new lines automatically, from 10 in steps of 10 by default. ESCAPE stops.

#### `LIST`

```
LIST [first][,last]
```

Lists the program. ESCAPE stops.

#### `LISTO`

```
LISTO n
```

Listing options: 1 space after the line number, 2 indent FOR loops, 4 indent REPEAT loops (add them up).

#### `*LIST`

```
*LIST           all
*LIST n         line n
*LIST n,        from line n
*LIST ,m        up to line m
*LIST n,m       lines n to m
```

Lists the program indented by its structure: two spaces per level of DEF PROC ... ENDPROC, a DEF FN that ends with a line starting "=", FOR ... NEXT and REPEAT ... UNTIL (LISTO 7 indents only the loops). The program itself is not changed; spaces at the start of its lines are replaced by the indentation. ESCAPE stops.

#### `DELETE`

```
DELETE first,last
```

Deletes program lines first to last.

#### `RENUMBER`

```
RENUMBER [start[,step]]
```

Renumbers the program, GOTO and GOSUB targets included.

#### `NEW`

```
NEW
```

Removes the program (OLD brings it back if nothing was typed in between).

#### `OLD`

```
OLD
```

Brings back a program after NEW or BREAK.

#### `RUN`

```
RUN
```

Runs the program, clearing the variables.

#### `CHAIN`

```
CHAIN "name"
```

Loads and runs a program.

#### `LOAD`

```
LOAD "name"
```

Loads a program (see FILES). For memory dumps see *LOAD.

#### `SAVE`

```
SAVE "name"
```

Saves the program (see FILES). For memory see *SAVE.

#### `CLEAR`

```
CLEAR
```

Removes all variables except the resident integers @% and A%-Z%.

#### `END`

```
END
```

Ends the program.

#### `STOP`

```
STOP
```

Stops the program with a message.

#### `REM`

```
REM text
```

A remark; the rest of the line is ignored.

#### `*SEARCH` (also `*FIND`, `FIND`, `*REPLACE`, `REPLACE`, `TOOLKIT`)

```
*SEARCH s1[,s2]   (asks Parameters)
*FIND s1          list the lines
*REPLACE s1,s2    replace, asking
```

Searches the program, as Beebug's Toolkit Plus: every line holding s1 is listed. With s2, each match may be replaced (Replace Y/N:). *SEARCH then asks for Parameters, letters typed together: C case ignored, D not in DATA, R not in REM, " not in strings, K s1 and s2 are keywords, G replace all without asking. # in s1 matches any character. Without K, keywords are not found (they are stored as tokens); line numbers after GOTO are never matched. A replacement clears the variables, as editing does.

```
*FIND count
*SEARCH PRINT,REPORT  (then K)
```

#### `*XREF` (also `*VARLIST`, `VARLIST`)

```
*XREF [R I S A F P H L]
*VARLIST          (as *XREF L)
```

Lists the variables, arrays, procedures and functions with their values and the lines that use them, as Beebug's Toolkit Plus. Letters choose: R reals, I integers, S strings, A arrays, F functions, P procedures (none: all); H values in hexadecimal, L no line numbers. Only what the program has made so far is known: run it first. A% to Z% are listed when the program uses them. Values are printed as PRINT would (@%).

#### `*CRUNCH` (also `*PACK`, `PACK`)

```
*CRUNCH [C R S :]   (also *PACK)
```

Makes the program shorter, as Beebug's Toolkit Plus: spaces, REM statements and extra colons go, and lines are joined. A letter switches that part off: C joining, R REMs, S spaces, : colons (B, L, T and V are accepted; brackets, LET, THEN and names are never changed). It asks first and prints the sizes; keep a copy. Lines named by GOTO, GOSUB or RESTORE keep their number (and their REM); lines are not joined after IF, ON, ELSE, DATA or a * command, nor are DEF and DATA lines joined on. Strings, DATA, * commands and assembler stay as they are. A computed GOTO's target is not known: use C there. Needs an REU.


## 6.3 Program flow

#### `IF`

```
IF cond [THEN] stmts [ELSE stmts]
```

Runs the statements when the condition is TRUE (not 0). The whole IF is one line.

#### `THEN`

```
IF cond THEN statements
```

Optional word in an IF line.

#### `ELSE`

```
IF cond THEN a ELSE b
```

The part of an IF line run when the condition is false. Also after ON ... GOTO.

#### `FOR`

```
FOR v=start TO end [STEP s]
...
NEXT [v]
```

Repeats the statements with v counting from start to end.

#### `TO`

```
FOR v=a TO b
```

The end value of a FOR loop.

#### `STEP`

```
FOR v=a TO b STEP s
```

The step of a FOR loop.

#### `NEXT`

```
NEXT [v]
```

Ends a FOR loop. See FOR.

#### `REPEAT`

```
REPEAT
...
UNTIL cond
```

Repeats until the condition is TRUE.

#### `UNTIL`

```
UNTIL cond
```

Ends a REPEAT loop.

#### `GOTO`

```
GOTO line
```

Continues at line.

#### `GOSUB`

```
GOSUB line
```

Calls the subroutine at line; RETURN comes back.

#### `RETURN`

```
RETURN
```

Ends a GOSUB subroutine.

#### `ON`

```
ON n GOTO l1,l2,... [ELSE ...]
ON n GOSUB l1,l2,...
```

Jumps to the n-th line in the list. See also ERROR.


## 6.4 Procedures and functions

Structured programs use `DEF PROC` and `DEF FN` with `LOCAL` variables
instead of `GOSUB`; see the example programs in `demos/`.

#### `DEF`

```
DEF PROCname[(params)]
DEF FNname[(params)]=expr
```

Defines a procedure or function. See PROC, FN.

#### `PROC`

```
DEF PROCname(params)
...
ENDPROC
PROCname(args)
```

A named procedure with its own LOCAL variables.

#### `ENDPROC`

```
ENDPROC
```

Ends a procedure. See PROC.

#### `FN`

```
DEF FNname(params)=expr
x=FNname(args)
```

A user-defined function; multi-line functions end with =value.

```
DEF FNsq(x)=x*x
PRINT FNsq(7)
```

#### `LOCAL`

```
LOCAL v[,v...]
```

Makes variables local to a procedure or function.


## 6.5 Errors

#### `ERRORS`

An error stops the program and prints a message; ON ERROR catches it. ERR gives the error number, ERL the line, REPORT prints the message.

Errors from the Ultimate keep the Ultimate's text with these numbers:

```
214  file not found
189  access denied
192  too many open files
199  other Ultimate errors
198  no room (LOAD too big)
222  channel not open
254  bad command
252  bad number
```

#### `ERROR`

```
ON ERROR statements
ON ERROR OFF
```

Statements to run when an error occurs. See ERRORS.

#### `ERR`

```
ERR
```

The number of the last error. See ERRORS.

#### `ERL`

```
ERL
```

The line number of the last error.

#### `REPORT`

```
REPORT
```

Prints the message of the last error.

#### `TRACE`

```
TRACE ON | TRACE OFF | TRACE n
```

Prints line numbers as they run (up to line n).


## 6.6 Numbers

#### `ABS`

```
ABS(n)
```

The absolute value of n.

```
PRINT ABS(-3.5)   gives 3.5
```

#### `SGN`

```
SGN(n)
```

-1, 0 or 1 by the sign of n.

#### `INT`

```
INT(n)
```

The largest whole number not above n.

#### `MOD`

```
a MOD b
```

The remainder of integer division.

#### `DIV`

```
a DIV b
```

Integer division.

```
PRINT 7 DIV 2    gives 3
```

#### `SQR`

```
SQR(n)
```

Square root.

#### `EXP`

```
EXP(n)
```

e to the power n.

#### `LN`

```
LN(n)
```

Natural logarithm.

#### `LOG`

```
LOG(n)
```

Logarithm base 10.

#### `SIN`

```
SIN(r)
```

Sine of r radians.

#### `COS`

```
COS(r)
```

Cosine of r radians.

#### `TAN`

```
TAN(r)
```

Tangent of r radians.

#### `ASN`

```
ASN(n)
```

Arc sine of n, in radians.

#### `ACS`

```
ACS(n)
```

Arc cosine of n, in radians.

#### `ATN`

```
ATN(n)
```

Arc tangent of n, in radians.

#### `DEG`

```
DEG(r)
```

Converts radians to degrees.

#### `RAD`

```
RAD(d)
```

Converts degrees to radians.

#### `PI`

```
PI
```

3.14159265.

#### `RND`

```
RND       random integer
RND(1)    0 to 1
RND(n)    1 to n
RND(-n)   sets the seed
```

Random numbers.

#### `AND`

```
a AND b
```

Bitwise AND of two integers; with comparisons a logical AND.

```
IF X>0 AND X<10 PRINT "OK"
```

#### `OR`

```
a OR b
```

Bitwise OR; with comparisons a logical OR.

#### `EOR`

```
a EOR b
```

Bitwise exclusive OR.

#### `NOT`

```
NOT n
```

Bitwise inversion; NOT TRUE is FALSE.

#### `TRUE`

```
TRUE
```

The value -1.

#### `FALSE`

```
FALSE
```

The value 0.


## 6.7 Strings

#### `ASC`

```
ASC(s$)
```

ASCII code of the first character of s$; -1 for an empty string.

#### `CHR$`

```
CHR$(n)
```

The character with code n.

```
PRINT CHR$(65)    gives A
```

#### `LEFT$`

```
LEFT$(s$,n)
```

The first n characters of s$.

#### `MID$`

```
MID$(s$,start[,n])
```

n characters of s$ from position start.

#### `RIGHT$`

```
RIGHT$(s$,n)
```

The last n characters of s$.

#### `LEN`

```
LEN(s$)
```

The length of s$.

#### `INSTR`

```
INSTR(a$,b$[,start])
```

The position of b$ in a$, or 0.

```
PRINT INSTR("HELLO","LL")   gives 3
```

#### `STR$`

```
STR$(n)
STR$~(n)
```

n as a string (decimal, or hexadecimal with ~).

#### `STRING$`

```
STRING$(n,s$)
```

s$ repeated n times.

#### `VAL`

```
VAL(s$)
```

The number at the start of s$.

#### `EVAL`

```
EVAL(s$)
```

Evaluates the expression in s$.

```
PRINT EVAL("2*21")   gives 42
```


## 6.8 Data in the program

#### `DATA`

```
DATA item[,item...]
```

Values for READ. See READ, RESTORE.

#### `READ`

```
READ v[,v...]
```

Reads the next DATA values.

#### `RESTORE`

```
RESTORE [line]
```

Lets READ start again at the first DATA, or at a line.


## 6.9 Keyboard and text on the screen

#### `PRINT`

```
PRINT [items]
```

Prints values. Separators: ; joins, , moves to the next field (set by @%), ' starts a new line. TAB(x) and SPC(n) position the cursor; ~ prints hexadecimal; a ; at the end keeps the cursor on the line.

```
PRINT "A=";A,~B;
```

#### `INPUT`

```
INPUT ["prompt",] v[,v...]
INPUT LINE a$
```

Reads values from the keyboard. INPUT LINE reads a whole line.

#### `GET`

```
k=GET
```

Waits for a key and returns its code. See KEYBOARD.

#### `GET$`

```
k$=GET$
```

Waits for a key and returns it as a string.

#### `INKEY`

```
k=INKEY(t)
```

Waits up to t centiseconds for a key; -1 if none came. INKEY(0) does not wait.

INKEY(-n) is TRUE while the key with the BBC's number n is held (the C64 key in its place): -1 SHIFT, -2 CTRL, -99 SPACE, -74 RETURN, -113 ESCAPE (RUN/STOP), -26 / -122 cursor left / right, -58 / -42 up / down, f1-f8 on F1-F7 (f2, f4, f6, f8 with Shift: -114 f1, -115 f2, -116 f3, -21 f4, -117 f5, -118 f6, -23 f7, -119 f8), -106 COPY (F1); letters and digits as on the BBC (-66 A, -98 Z, ...). Keys the C64 lacks (f0, f9, TAB, CAPS LOCK, [ ]) are never held. INKEY(-256) gives 255: a BBC B with OS 1.2.

```
IF INKEY(-98) THEN X%=X%-1
```

#### `INKEY$`

```
k$=INKEY$(t)
```

As INKEY, returning a string (empty if no key).

#### `TAB`

```
PRINT TAB(x)
PRINT TAB(x,y)
```

Moves to column x, or to column x of row y.

#### `SPC`

```
PRINT SPC(n)
```

Prints n spaces.

#### `POS`

```
POS
```

The column of the text cursor.

#### `VPOS`

```
VPOS
```

The row of the text cursor.

#### `COUNT`

```
COUNT
```

The number of characters printed since the last new line.

#### `WIDTH`

```
WIDTH n
```

Starts a new line after n characters (WIDTH 0: off).

#### `CLS`

```
CLS
```

Clears the text screen.

#### `COLOUR` (also `COLOR`)

```
COLOUR n
```

Sets the text colour (n) or background (128+n). See COLOURS.

On the text screen COLOUR 128+n prints the following characters in reverse video in colour n (black text on a coloured bar); COLOUR 128 ends it. The whole screen's background is VDU 19,0,n,0,0,0.


## 6.10 Time

#### `TIME`

```
TIME
TIME=n
```

A clock counting centiseconds; can be set. It keeps real time at every CPU speed. For the date and time see *TIME.


## 6.11 Machine code

BBC BASIC has an assembler built in (`[` ... `]`). Zero page &70-&8F is
free for your own machine code, as on a BBC Micro; the MOS entry points
are in chapter 13.

#### `ASSEMBLER`

BBC BASIC contains a 6502 assembler. Square brackets enclose assembly language; P% is the address to assemble at; OPT sets listing and errors.

```
10 DIM C% 20
20 FOR Z%=0 TO 2 STEP 2
30 P%=C%:[OPT Z%
40 LDA #65:JSR &C7EE:RTS
50 ]:NEXT
60 CALL C%
```

OPT 0 assembles silently; OPT 2 reports errors; add 1 to list. Two passes resolve forward references. Labels start with a dot.

**U64:** OSWRCH is &C7EE, not &FFEE (see *HELP MOS). Zero page &70-&8F is free for your code.

#### `OPT`

```
[OPT n
```

Assembler option. See ASSEMBLER.

#### `CALL`

```
CALL address[,params]
```

Calls machine code. A, X, Y and the carry come from A%, X%, Y% and C%.

#### `USR`

```
x=USR(address)
```

Calls machine code and returns A, X, Y and P packed in an integer. See CALL.

#### `OSCLI`

```
OSCLI string
```

Runs a * command from a string, so it can contain variables.

```
OSCLI "TURBO "+STR$(S%)
```
